model_output.score_comment_short: The internship names useful tools and audiences, but leaves the work itself brief.
model_output.score_comment_long: The Tableau dashboard and member survey work establish a practical analytics foundation. Most bullets stop before explaining what you analyzed or reported. Add the dashboard's subject and an example finding first.
model_output.score_plain: A reviewer can identify an analytics internship, but may need more detail to understand what you can contribute in a similar role.
model_output.first_impression: Your information degree and credit union internship point toward entry-level analytics. The internship bullets name Excel, SQL and Tableau, but give little detail about the analyses.
model_output.biggest_gap_example: "Built a dashboard in Tableau for the marketing team" doesn't say what the dashboard tracked, so its purpose remains unclear.
model_output.summary: Building a Tableau dashboard for a marketing team is useful to keep because it connects your analysis work to a specific audience. Your internship also includes survey data cleaning, reporting and a presentation, which together fit an early-career analytics profile. The degree coursework reinforces that direction. What you found in the data is still unclear, making it difficult to assess the substance of your analysis.
strengths: Excel and SQL are tied to member survey data rather than appearing only in a skills list.
Weekly reporting shows a recurring responsibility during the credit union internship.
The treasurer role adds budget and reimbursement responsibilities alongside your technical work.
gaps: The dashboard's subject and intended use aren't named, leaving its business context unclear.
The survey bullet doesn't describe the data problems you addressed, so the cleaning work is difficult to distinguish.
The presentation mentions findings without identifying one, leaving your analytical conclusions out of view.
